svg.title: Yomika tray mark
svg.desc: The brand mark re-derived for the Windows notification area. Same rounded plate and same two-tier ink as `yomika-mark-print.svg`, but the glyph is filled instead of stroked and reduced from five elements to three: at the 16px the tray actually gives it, the print mark's 18-unit strokes land on 0.56px and the whole thing dissolves into grey mush (user report: "在小尺寸下很难看清"). Every edge here sits on a 32-unit boundary, so a 512-unit master downsamples 1:2 to the 32px tray bitmap and 1:32 to a 16px render on exact pixel boundaries — the 128-unit stroke is a full 4px, the dot 5px across. The dot's box ends on the 448 lines and starts 96 units off the arm, so its tangents land on the grid too rather than blurring over half a pixel. The spine is the one edge that steps off that grid: it sits at x=88 rather than 64, because measured gaps of 64 all round still read as a tight left edge (user report: "左侧空隙还是太小了"). The left edge of the mark is a flat, full-height bar whose optical extent *is* its bounding box; the right edge is a circle, which the eye reads as ending inside its box by roughly a fifth of its radius. 88 units against 64 makes the two sides read equal — 4px against 3px at the 24px this machine's tray uses, 5px against 4px at 32px — and the half-pixel the 88 leaves at 32px anti-aliases into *softer* ink on the flat side, which is the side that needed the air. The accent frame is dropped, not forgotten: at 16px it stole the width the glyph needs (candidate "C-framed" in the tray-icon study), and the plate already carries the identity.
